completion_conditions: A ledger the loop writes after its last delivery point is carried by the next branch-state sync.
A file that was already delivered is never carried twice, and the carry is idempotent.
The carry never picks up a file belonging to another task's contract or any non-ledger mirror record it was not asked to deliver.
The full suite, the goal-loop suite and validate_shiki stay green.

decisions: MEASURED. After each goal completed, the coordinator checkout held ledger files absent from main — e.g. `L-20260805T073358816023Z-baf26752` (type `mergegate`, 'Goal loop merged PR #289 ...') and `L-20260805T073400360295Z-ec8cb045` (type `check`, 'Goal loop marked T-... done: PR already merged'). `git merge origin/main` then aborted with 'The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge', and continuing required backing the files up and deleting them by hand. That happened on 2026-08-05 (twice), and again on 2026-08-06 (twice).

MECHANISM, read from source. `_sync_state_to_branch` (`scripts/shiki_loop.py:1000`) is the ONLY delivery path, and it is called from exactly three effectors: `:1850` (create_pr), `:1890` (dispatch_repair), `:1954` (rerun_cca). The `merge` and `mark_done` effectors (`:2011-2013`) append ledgers and never sync. By then the task branch is merged, so there is nothing left to sync to.

SCOPE OF THE HARM, stated honestly. No dangling reference reaches main: the task file on main references only the entries that were delivered, so `validate_shiki` and MergeGate stay green, and GitHub — source of truth #1 — records the merge itself durably. What is lost is the mirror's record of the loop's own final actions, and what is PAID is a manual conflict resolution on every subsequent sync. This is a mirror-completeness and operability defect, not an evidence-integrity one, and the contract should not overstate it.

REJECTED — reordering the closeout so the entries can ride it. `docs/adr/0012` pins the closeout decision table, and the closeout merge record cannot exist before the closeout is merged. Reordering is a governance change for a bookkeeping problem.

CHOSEN — a self-healing carry. Record post-closeout bookkeeping as undelivered, and have the next branch-state sync — for any task, in any goal — carry every undelivered loop-authored ledger file. That matches what the manual 'carry ... ledger evidence onto the task branch' commits already in this repository's history do by hand, needs no reordering and no ADR change. The lag is bounded and self-clearing; the final entries of the final goal remain undelivered until the next goal runs, which must be stated rather than hidden.

LOCK-SUFFICIENCY CHECK (2026-08-06). MUST-CHANGE: `scripts/shiki_loop.py`; `tests/test_dispatch_state_sync.py` (7 references — owns the sync property); `tests/test_loop_branch_plumbing.py` (12 references — the heaviest driver, imports the sync internals directly).

TWO DESIGN CONSTRAINTS THAT KEEP THE LOCK SET AT THREE, both measured. (a) Implement the carry inside `_sync_state_to_branch`, NOT inside `_evidence_relatives_for_task`: `tests/test_mirror_lock_injection.py` calls that function directly at `:320`, `:336`, `:498` and asserts on its output, so changing what it returns would pull that file in. (b) Do not change `_sync_state_to_branch`'s signature: `tests/test_loop_tdd_evidence.py:209-224` monkeypatches it.

MUST-NOT-BREAK (verification command, not locks): `tests/test_mirror_lock_injection.py`, `tests/test_loop_tdd_evidence.py`, `tests/test_loop_lock_guard.py` (prose reference only), and `scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh` which drives the loop end to end. `scripts/shiki_tasks.py:39` and `scripts/mergegate_check.py:190` mention the sync in COMMENTS describing what rides a branch; they are not code references and must not be edited.

Risk is medium and honest: this changes which files a state sync commits, not what any gate enforces, and no approval source, schema or workflow moves. Under `.shiki/guardian-policy.json` (`applies_to_risk: [high, critical]`) neither PR triggers the Guardian gate.

non_goals: Reordering the closeout, or changing the decision table docs/adr/0012 pins.
Carrying anything other than loop-authored ledger files that were never delivered.
Changing any gate, schema, workflow or approval source.
Touching any file outside the declared locks.
outcome: The ledger entries the goal loop writes AFTER its last delivery point — the closeout merge and the mark-done — stop accumulating only in the coordinator checkout. Measured four times on 2026-08-05/06: each left the coordinator's mirror diverged from main, and every subsequent `git merge origin/main` aborted with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten', requiring a manual back-up-and-delete before work could continue.

amendments: 2026-08-06 SCOPE AMENDMENT, from the pre-PR reviewer's blocking findings on the first implementation attempt and a re-measurement of the original symptom. Both the chosen design and the diagnosis were wrong. (1) THE CARRY IS FORBIDDEN BY MERGEGATE, not merely awkward. ledger_entry_allowed_for_task (mergegate_check.py:2408-2413) admits an entry onto a task PR only when entry.task_id == the PR's task_id, or when the entry has NO task_id and its goal_id matches. The loop's post-merge bookkeeping entries DO carry the completed task's task_id, so they can ride only that task's own PR - which no longer exists. Carrying them onto any other task's branch makes enforce_untrusted_shiki_mutations block with 'PR changes ledger ... not listed in current task ledger_evidence' (mergegate_check.py:2738), which would fail EVERY subsequent PR in the repository. The reviewer caught this before a PR existed. (2) THE MEASURED SYMPTOM HAS A DIFFERENT CAUSE. The aborting merges were re-measured file by file: 27 of 28 and 20 of 20 of the colliding files were BYTE-IDENTICAL to origin/main - already delivered through the task branch. The genuinely undelivered entries never collided. The cause is not undelivered evidence; it is that the loop writes mirror files into the COORDINATOR checkout and never adds them to that checkout's index, so git refuses when the same paths later arrive through origin/main. AMENDED SCOPE: make the loop stop leaving untracked mirror copies in the coordinator checkout that collide with the same paths arriving from the default branch. The delivery mechanism is unchanged - _sync_state_to_branch keeps doing exactly what it does today - and no cross-task or cross-goal carry is introduced. REMOVED FROM SCOPE: the undelivered-marker, the cross-goal carry, and its idempotence and foreign-record tests. RECORDED, NOT FIXED: the loop's own final ledger entries for a completed goal remain absent from main. Measured harm of that: none - the task file on main references only delivered entries, validate_shiki and MergeGate stay green, and GitHub records the merge durably. Delivering them would need a vehicle MergeGate permits, which per (1) is a PR for the same task, i.e. a second closeout - separate work, not justified by the measured harm.

tasks.scope:
The goal loop leaves mirror files it wrote in the COORDINATOR checkout untracked, and never adds them to that checkout's index. When the same paths later arrive through `git merge origin/main` - which is how they come back after the task PR merges - git aborts with 'The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge', and continuing requires backing the files up and deleting them by hand. Measured four times on 2026-08-05/06 while driving this repository's own backlog.

Make the loop stop producing that collision. The delivery mechanism is UNCHANGED: `_sync_state_to_branch` (`scripts/shiki_loop.py:1000`) keeps copying the evidence set onto the task branch exactly as it does today, and NO cross-task or cross-goal carry is introduced.

WHY NO CARRY - this is the load-bearing constraint, and the first implementation attempt was blocked on it by the pre-PR reviewer before a PR existed. `ledger_entry_allowed_for_task` (`scripts/mergegate_check.py:2408-2413`) admits a ledger entry onto a task PR only when `entry.task_id == task_id`, or when the entry has no task_id and `entry.goal_id == goal_id`. The loop's post-merge bookkeeping entries carry the completed task's own task_id, so they can ride only that task's PR - which no longer exists. Carrying one onto another task's branch makes `enforce_untrusted_shiki_mutations` block with 'PR changes ledger ... not listed in current task ledger_evidence' (`:2738`), which would fail EVERY subsequent PR in the repository.

WHAT THE FIX MAY NOT DO: it must not delete or move any ledger, task, lock, runner or worktree record as a way of avoiding the collision - the mirror is append-only evidence. It must not change what `_sync_state_to_branch` copies, its signature (tests/test_loop_tdd_evidence.py:209-224 monkeypatches it) or what `_evidence_relatives_for_task` returns (tests/test_mirror_lock_injection.py asserts on it at :320, :336, :498). It must not touch any gate, schema, workflow or approval source.

TESTS. `tests/test_dispatch_state_sync.py`: after a sync, the coordinator checkout has no untracked file whose path also exists on the default branch. `tests/test_loop_branch_plumbing.py`: reproduce the measured sequence against a real repository - run a task to the point where the loop has written its mirror records, bring the same paths in from the default branch, and assert the merge succeeds rather than aborting; assert it is still true after a second cycle.

REPRODUCIBILITY - what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: `git merge origin/main` in the coordinator checkout aborts with 'The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge', naming ledger, runner and worktree files the loop wrote.
  Measured four times on 2026-08-05/06. Re-measured file by file: 27 of 28, and 20 of 20, of the colliding files were BYTE-IDENTICAL to origin/main - they had already been delivered through the task branch. The genuinely undelivered entries never collided at all.
  Root cause: the loop writes into the coordinator checkout's working tree and never stages those writes there, so git treats a delivered-and-returning file as an untracked file it must not overwrite.
  Why not a carry: MergeGate forbids it - see above; the first attempt was blocked by the reviewer for exactly this reason.
  Recorded, not fixed: the loop's own final ledger entries for a completed goal remain absent from main. Measured harm: none - the task file on main references only delivered entries, validate_shiki and MergeGate stay green, and GitHub records the merge durably.
  Reproducible when: the measured sequence completes without a manual back-up-and-delete, twice in a row.
